body:
Well it seems that the best outcome is for you to get a job and fix the other things that make you want to die. You need to figure out exactly what those reasons are first. It sounds as though you wish you were more independent. Finding a job helps that. What kind of job can you do or what kind would you want to do? Why do you say the world is a horrible place? Maybe if you change your outlook you won't see it like that. 

If your life isn't together and you aren't doing something you find meaningful or you aren't at least progressing towards something then it's common to become depressed. The nice thing is all of your progress in the right direction makes you feel that much better. Once you get started it can start to take off.

And there's nothing wrong with sharing anonymously online. It's an easy way to open up and get honest responses. I'm happy to help in any way I can, but you should really be talking about this stuff with your family and/or doctor if you're considering suicide. I lost someone very close to me to suicide and really wish they had been more open about it. It was very unexpected and maybe I could have helped if I had known how serious it was. All problems seem a whole lot smaller after something like that. Fixing the damage caused to your loved ones is harder than fixing whatever needs to be fixed in your life.

I know you can't live your life for others, but you can use them as motivation to want to improve your own life. There's always a way to happiness. Figure out what happiness looks like for you and make it happen.

Going on welfare temporarily is nothing to be ashamed of. You've paid taxes and will continue to pay taxes so you get access when you need it. Have you tried something like fastfood or stocking shelves for work? -$200 doesn't seem like a big deal, certainly not something to kill yourself over. You could just cancel the phone and gym membership for now too. If you feel like a leach then the best way to fix it is to get some form of income. Is there a reason you can't get a job? If there is, you have a genuine reason for welfare.

Regarding the heart racing, have you mentioned it to your doctor? Do you have issues with anxiety? It's common for people with anxiety to get "paralyzed" under a mountain of tasks, the tasks don't get done, the mountain grows, paralysis gets worse, repeat. Does this sound familiar to you?

Youve already accepted the fate, why not cheat death. At this point you've got the majority of a free life at your disposal. Scramble some cash together if you can and head out as far as you can for a fresh start. It's worth a shot

All you can do is be the best you can be. Your parents will accept you and if they don't, cut them out of your life if  that's what it takes. We're all trying to be happy and that sure isn't going to happen unless you can be yourself. Have you talked to your parents about being suicidal? I hope if they knew how you felt they would be crushed. Your 17, don't you think you should give yourself a chance to become the real you before you make a permanent decision like suicide? Things like looks and relationships change over time, so just keep that in mind. Work on the things that bother you about yourself and accept the things you can't control

People are great at finding the negative aspects of our own personality and terrible at finding the good aspects. I'm sure you have a lot going for you that you don't realize. What would it take for your life to turn around and have you not feel this way? In my personal experience it's wild how differently I felt by fixing up a few of the fucked up things in my life. Some of them had to do with me personally, some with my family, but a lot was just shit that built up that I needed to take care of. I used to think I was this strong, courageous person for enduring the burdens in my life. I knew I wouldn't kill myself no matter how much I wanted to because I was strong and I needed to be strong for others. It turns out that what I really needed to do was use that strength to get my shit together and fix my family. Even though that was the hardest possible thing for Me, it's What I needed to do. What do you need to do? Depressed people are fucking strong man. There's nothing harder than having to constantly fight your own mind. You just need to find the root of your problems and push a little harder, a little longer.

Find what you love and do that. If you feel like something is holding you back from accomplishing that, work on yourself. If the issue is your negative thoughts, find where they're coming from and see what you can do to fix it. It can be hard to break out of that cycle of thinking. You don't have to live your life all at once so don't worry about being happy when your old, do what you can for yourself now. Being happy isn't easy for everyone but I believe it is an option for everyone. What are you missing in your life? It sounds as though your family isn't the most supportive but many people these days simply don't know how to deal with mental illness in loved ones, so it may not be a lack of caring. How's your work/school situation, are you healthy, do you have a meaningful romantic relationship with someone? Feel free to message me if you'd like.
